items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: INTERVIEWER: 'I met her the other day and she remembered you actually.' / INTERVIEWEE: 'Yeah, yeah, well, he played a while with us.' (Context implies the interviewee knew George Zeno and his partner Emma Zeno through George's music career, but no direct personal interaction between interviewee and

ctx.x: Think you can make a good planet player. So what I did, I talked him up and I let him play a couple of pieces. I said, well, how do you make your sharks and how do you make your flat? They ain't nothing but natural. No, they ain't but six holes. You see. He told me when I want to make a shark like that, he said, I want to make a shark like that. He said, I lose the top of the hole and I blow hard. And when I want to make a flat, he said, I just cover half of the hole. So, I called himself, I said, you know what…

But was this where he was living? That's where he was living at that time. Was he living there with his wife then or with his mother? Well, he had a wife, a common old wife. Yes, I know who you mean actually because her name is Emma. Emma. Emma Zeno. Emma Zeno. And I met her the other day and she remembered you actually. She remembered me. Yes, I was asking her about who she remembered of the musicians that George played with and you were about the only one she remembered.

Yeah, yeah. Well, he played a while with us. He played a while with us because it didn't take him no time. He used to practice by himself, you know. I tried to get him to learn how to read. He couldn't read no music.
